samples.identification: Unsigned Rust encrypted Python-runtime extractor, config.exe / Security Update Module
samples.reason: The encrypted ZIP replaces CPython encodings/__init__.pyc with a bootstrap that joins encoded shellcode, maps an anonymous executable section, copies the code, and calls it. A legitimate security update does not replace Python codec initialization with this native payload. Renamed signed Python and Squirrel binaries supply the execution chain. No family attribution is established.
deployment_context_missing: Runtime success and final shellcode payload identity

execution_trace.effect: Rust main calls console hiding, elevation checking, archive copy/decryption/extraction, and child launch.
OpenProcessToken(TOKEN_QUERY), GetTokenInformation(TokenElevation), ShellExecuteW with runas when not elevated. This requests UAC consent; no UAC bypass is established.
Base64 password and hex salt/nonce/tag; PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 137539 iterations and a 32-byte key; AES-GCM authentication succeeds during offline recovery.
ZIP parsing and filesystem extraction to default C:/ProgramData/python (overridable output argument).
Constructs C:/ProgramData/python/wefault.exe and starts it via the Rust process implementation/CreateProcessW.

recovered_chain: Root wefault.exe is a signed Squirrel StubExecutable identifying MongoDBCompass, which selects app-1.49.1/wefault.exe.
App wefault.exe is byte-identical to the official CPython 3.10.0 pythonw.exe; Python DLLs, ctypes extension, libffi and VC runtime also match the official embeddable ZIP.
python310.zip differs; encodings/__init__.pyc is replaced. xdis 3.10 disassembly shows import-time execute_shellcode(shellcode).

execute_shellcode creates a pagefile-backed mapping with protection 0x40, maps it with FILE_MAP_WRITE|FILE_MAP_EXECUTE, memmoves the byte array, constructs CFUNCTYPE(None)(address), and calls the resulting pointer. Finally it unmaps the view and closes the handle.

The 257414-byte native payload uses a tail decoder and a descending XOR/add-feedback loop. Bounded Unicorn emulation executes only arithmetic decoding and stops at an unmapped GS/TEB read. Recovered code walks the PEB and has flattened API-resolution control flow. No C2 endpoint, persistence action, theft or ransomware action is established.
The separate invalid-magic base32.pyc is an additional opaque native-code-looking artifact; it is not treated as executed without a proven reference.
samples.coverage_gap: The original PE remains 0 hostile / 1 suspicious. Its embedded ZIP is AES-GCM ciphertext, and Cleave does not run this custom decryptor or propagate the recovered stage back to the original file. The decoded bootstrap has two distinct hostile detections (encoded native execution and trusted codec-bootstrap replacement). A third independent hostile action is not established. Generic UAC consent, hiding, crypto and launch primitives are not promoted to hostile.
samples.classifier_gap: Original PE stays unflagged at calibrated level -1 despite probability rising from 0.7409244 to 0.8860738. Recovered ZIP changes from unflagged (0.5399861) to flagged (0.9999968, level 0, confidence 100) after the new rules.

samples.identification: BusyBox ash/hush source5.tests, collected as source2.tests
samples.reason: Byte-for-byte match to BusyBox 1.36.1 source5.tests. Writes a one-line positional-argument printer, invokes the selected test shell twice with dot-source commands and different argument lists, prints exit status, and removes the created file. No obfuscation, network or unrelated payload.
samples.changes: Adds notable variable-shell source-command coverage; preserves the accurate local deletion trait.
samples.external_label_explanation: The collection name differs from upstream. A parent-corpus label or classifier error could explain the malware label, but the source of that mislabel is unknown. THIS_SH is provided by the test harness; an arbitrary substituted interpreter is not evidence against these upstream bytes.

samples.reason: Byte-for-byte match to BusyBox 1.36.1 shift.right. The six lines are expected stdout from shift.tests, which echoes positional arguments around successful and out-of-range shift operations. The file itself is expected output, not evidence of process execution.
samples.changes: Preserves relative-command text as metadata/lang/source/syntax/command instead of claiming process creation. Its download/chmod/execute consumer retains the same matcher.
samples.external_label_explanation: Likely corpus contamination or source-context loss; precise labeling provenance is unavailable.

rule_corrections: config.exe internal/original version fields moved from masquerade objectives to PE resource metadata; no matcher or PE scope loss. Removed inherited ATT&CK masquerade mapping from the neutral observations.

Zstandard bytes at file offset 0x77c33 are a codec magic constant copied/compared in code, not an embedded compressed frame. Preserve the exact matcher/scope as instruction-operand metadata and update the existing compression-profile consumer.

liblzma, lzma_ prefix, CRC64-table name, and LZMA_OK support codec presence, not compression direction. Move exact matchers, scopes and exclusions into data/codec. Update direct references and preserve ancestor membership in compression composites. The LzmaEnc compression rule stays in its original direction-specific leaf.

Relative command-shaped plain text does not prove execution. Relocate exactly, retain severity/count bounds, and update the direct hostile text-dropper consumer. Ancestor consumers were checked; they either exclude text or require independent conditions absent from this sample.
limitations: New bytecode call-sequence matcher is explicitly Python 3.10 and retains its supported local-variable layout. Other bytecode versions/layouts need separate evidence-backed support.
Only two distinct hostile findings are justified for the recovered bootstrap. Propagation to the inner and outer ZIP produces six file-level hostile records, not six independent behaviors.
No shared matcher was weakened, no severity was reduced, and retention checks found no material detection loss after ID normalization.

micro-behaviors/data/compress selectors in both compression-evidence composites
